# Frozen goal-migration inputs

These executable SQL definitions were frozen from JobDB `f85c24f`, whose
`schema.go` still supports legacy formats 11/12. Tests execute these files
directly against temporary on-disk SQLite files. They do not call the current
runtime constructor to manufacture a supposed historical schema.

- `goal-format-11.sql`: exact base job/cell/goal/candidate/dependency/preparation
  definitions and indexes, plus the format-11 marker.
- `goal-lease-events.sql`: optional format-11 and required format-12 extension.
- `goal-receipts.sql`: optional accepted selected-submission receipt extension.

Format-12 cases combine the frozen base with the event extension and set the
marker to 12 without invoking a normalizing constructor. Optional-extension
cases also exercise their absence. Keep these files frozen when the live schema
changes; add supported historical variants explicitly rather than regenerating
them from future constants.

Semantic fixtures populate real legacy columns/payloads with hidden primary
members, sequential terminal attempts, inherited active overlaps, original
ownership differing from current presentation, explicit failure snapshots,
historical secondary links and cross-primary settled producers, pending indexed
waits, unpublished preparations and accepted receipts. Historical links are
saved legacy data, not a new consumer dependency on the retiring attachment API.
The checker continues testing files without initializing them through the live
constructor. Converter tests additionally use the frozen runtime-produced input
below to verify actual conversion, retained readers, replay and admission.
Boundary-injection tests verify transactional rollback and rerun. These local
fixtures do not establish a deployed conversion or external blob preservation.

## Runtime-produced preservation fixture

`goal-runtime-11.sql` was generated by public operations on saved source
`5732636605cb6f9e7e30fc4f2c5fd230d43ce9f7` in an isolated checkout. It
contains real initial/completion chapters, inline input artifact bytes, lease
events, shared restart, primary selection receipt, hidden cancellation, legacy
failure/settled dependency and an exact-integer tenant configuration. Tests load
the same frozen definitions as formats 11 and 12 (this 11 input includes events).
Generation used VACUUM INTO followed by Python sqlite3 iterdump; only transaction
wrappers were removed and an explicit format marker was appended. Identity and
blob values are retained verbatim. It supplements the synthetic edge-case
fixtures and does not stand for a deployed database or external artifact store.

## Current upstream writer fixture

`goal-upstream-11.sql` was generated by the public runtime at
`1dd75e9fd864d05c5b102781af4d8671519a5655`. Its actual marker is 11; it includes
additive append fields/events and has no schedule objects. It preserves a
nanosecond delayed submission with an inline artifact and an existing append
chain. Tests compare every original job column and rowid, reopen, inspect the
artifact and availability, and continue the same append generation. A variant
adds dormant historical schedule data and checks preservation. Separate negative
variants reject broken append identity/generation or partial append columns
without changing definitions or data. A format-12 event-extension fixture checks
custom indexes/triggers, dependent views/foreign keys and the allocator high-water
mark while expanding the event constraint to accept append acquisition.
